cases.sentence: На ___, когда Одинцова явилась к чаю, Базаров долго сидел, нагнувшись над своею чашкою, да вдруг взглянул на нее…
cases.explain: «следующий день» — after the preposition «на», the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: When Madame Odintsov entered the breakfast-room next morning, Bazarov had been sitting over his cup for a considerable time. He glanced sharply at her as she opened the door, and she turned in his direction as inevitably as though he had signed to her to do so. Somehow her face looked pale, and it was not long before she returned to her boudoir, whence she issued again only at luncheon time. Since dawn the weather had been too rainy to admit of outdoor expeditions, and therefore the party adjourned to the drawing-room, where Arkady began to read aloud the latest number of some journal, while the Princess manifested her usual surprise at his conduct (as though it had been conduct of an indecent nature!), and fixed upon him a gaze which, though one of lasting malignancy, proved also to be one of which he took not the slightest notice.

cases.explain: «скорыми шагами» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: Meanwhile Madame Odintsov walked hurriedly to her boudoir, and Bazarov followed with his eyes fixed upon the floor, and his ears open to no sound but the faint rustling of a silk dress. Arrived at her destination, Madame seated herself in the chair which she had occupied overnight, and Bazarov also took a seat where he had sat on the occasion in question.

cases.sentence: Базаров проворно следовал за нею, не поднимая глаз и только ловя слухом ___ и шелест скользившего перед ним шелкового платья.
cases.explain: «тонкий свист» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: Meanwhile Madame Odintsov walked hurriedly to her boudoir, and Bazarov followed with his eyes fixed upon the floor, and his ears open to no sound but the faint rustling of a silk dress. Arrived at her destination, Madame seated herself in the chair which she had occupied overnight, and Bazarov also took a seat where he had sat on the occasion in question.

cases.explain: «косвенный взгляд» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: "Happiness, I think," she said. "In fact, I was speaking to you of myself. The reason why I mention happiness is the following. Why is it that when one is enjoying, say, a piece of music, or a beautiful summer evening, or a conversation with a sympathetic companion, the occasion seems rather a hint at an infinite felicity existent elsewhere than a real felicity actually being experienced? Perhaps, however, you have never encountered such a phenomenon?"

cases.sentence: Вам известно, что я занимаюсь ___, а кто я…
cases.explain: «естественными науками» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: "I am surprised! Already you know that I dabble in natural science; while, as regards my future——" "Yes? As regards your future?"

cases.explain: «уездный лекарь» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: "Wait. Do you mean to tell me that such a modest rôle will really satisfy you, when you yourself have asserted that the science of medicine does not exist? No, no! You have given me that answer for the reason that you desire to keep me at arm's length, that you have no faith in me. Then let me tell you that I am capable of understanding you, that I too have known poverty and ambition, that I too have had my experiences."

cases.explain: «небольшого колебания» — after the preposition «после», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: "I could," came the reply after a brief hesitation. Bazarov bowed in an ironical manner.

cases.sentence: – Как хотите, – продолжала она, – а мне все-таки что-то говорит, что мы сошлись недаром, что мы будем ___.
cases.explain: «хорошими друзьями» — the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: "Very well," she said. "Yet I will venture to say that you and I have not met in vain, and that we shall always remain good friends. Moreover, I feel certain that in time your secretiveness and reserve will disappear."

cases.sentence: Но это было не трепетание юношеской робости, не ___ первого признания овладел им: это страсть в нем билась, сильная и тяжелая – страсть, похожая на злобу и, быть может, сродни ей…
cases.explain: «сладкий ужас» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: She stretched out her arms before her, while Bazarov, turning, pressed his forehead against the window-pane. His breath caught in his throat, and his whole body was quivering. Yet this was not the agitation born of the diffidence of youth, nor was it the awe inspired by a first confession of love. Rather, it was the beating of a strong and terrible emotion which resembled madness and was, perhaps, akin to it. As for Madame Odintsov, a great horror had come over her—also a great feeling of compassion for him.

cases.sentence: Но это было не трепетание юношеской робости, не сладкий ужас ___ овладел им: это страсть в нем билась, сильная и тяжелая – страсть, похожая на злобу и, быть может, сродни ей…
cases.explain: «первого признания» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: She stretched out her arms before her, while Bazarov, turning, pressed his forehead against the window-pane. His breath caught in his throat, and his whole body was quivering. Yet this was not the agitation born of the diffidence of youth, nor was it the awe inspired by a first confession of love. Rather, it was the beating of a strong and terrible emotion which resembled madness and was, perhaps, akin to it. As for Madame Odintsov, a great horror had come over her—also a great feeling of compassion for him.

cases.sentence: – Вы меня не поняли, – прошептала она с ___.
cases.explain: «торопливым испугом» — after the preposition «с», the instrumental marks the means, company, or complement.
cases.translation: "You have mistaken me!" Had he taken another step, she would have screamed. Biting his lips, he left the room.

cases.sentence: Под влиянием различных смутных чувств, сознания уходящей жизни, желания новизны она заставила себя дойти до ___, заставила себя заглянуть за нее – и увидала за ней даже не бездну, а пустоту… или безобразие.
cases.explain: «известной черты» — after the preposition «до», the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Nor had her sangfroid really been shattered. Rather, she was a little agitated—so little that, when, for some unknown reason, she shed a tear or two, those tears owed their origin not to any deep emotion, to the fact that she was wounded, but to a sense of having involuntarily been at fault in permitting certain vague yearnings—a certain consciousness of the transience of life, a certain desire for novelty—to urge her towards the boundary line. And over that boundary line she had peeped. And in front of her she had beheld, not an abyss, but a waste, a sheer ugliness.
